summary: The root سَتَتَ (sattata) primarily means to cover or conceal something. It implies drawing a veil or screen over an object, making it hidden from view.

headwords.def: سَتَّهُ , [aor. سَتُتَ , accord to rule, and inf. n. app. سَتٌّ , q. v.,] He attributed or imputed to him, or charged him with, or accused him of, a fault, or defect, or the like; as also سَدَّهُ ; syn. عَابَهُ . (TA. [The sense in which عابه is there used is indicated by the context.])

headwords.def: سَتٌ a dial. var. of اِسْتٌ : see the latter word in art. سته , in two places.
سَتٌّ Foul, or evil, speech or language. (IAar, K.) And also, [like سَدٌّ ,] A fault, or defect, or the like; syn. عَيْبٌ . (K.)

headwords.gloss: Sixty; one of the tenfold numbers; Sixtieth
headwords.def: سِتُّونَ [ Sixty, ] one of the tenfold numbers, (M, TA,) namely, that between خَمْسُونَ and سَبْعُونَ , (TA,) is derived from سِتٌّ . (M, TA.) [Also Sixtieth. ]
